answer: I'd like to talk about something very ordinary that sits on our kitchen counter. A genuinely useful object in my home is my electric kettle, which I honestly could not do without. It is a simple steel one that my younger sister and I bought for the family a couple of years ago. It might sound trivial, but as someone who drinks tea several times a day, it is completely [[indispensable]]. I use it mainly to boil water for tea, but my mother also uses it when she needs hot water for cooking, and my sister makes instant noodles with it during late-night study sessions. I use it first thing in the morning, throughout the day, and last thing at night. On a typical day it must be switched on six or seven times, especially when guests drop by, which happens a lot in our household. What makes it so useful is how quickly and efficiently it boils water, saving me a lot of time. Before I had it, using the stove felt slow and [[cumbersome]] by comparison. It is also wonderfully [[convenient]], with an automatic switch-off that means I never have to watch it. Such a simple [[appliance]] has become woven into my daily routine without my even noticing. Honestly, it is a perfect example of how the most ordinary objects are often the most useful. I think we tend to overlook these everyday items, yet they quietly make life far more [[manageable]]. If it broke tomorrow, I would replace it immediately without a second thought.

followUps.q: Who else in your family uses the kettle?
followUps.answer: Pretty much everyone. My mother uses it while cooking, my younger sister relies on it during late-night study sessions, and my father makes his afternoon tea with it now that he's retired.

followUps.q: Is there anything about it you would improve?
followUps.answer: Perhaps the size. When relatives visit, we have to boil water two or three times for everyone's tea, so a slightly larger one would be more [[practical]] for a household like ours.
